title: SDK integration walkthrough - Prism Payments
summary: AE + SE walked Prism Payments through Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth patterns (API key, short-lived tokens, KMS), environment setup for hosted vs. private deployments, and a simple sample app. Customer requested a pilot repo, security docs, and a short benchmark run; agreed to follow up with pricing and onboarding steps.
topics: Auth: API key vs short-lived tokens vs KMS
Environment variables and local dev setup
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro: I'm Aisha, AE at Redwood, with Diego from SE.   
[00:08] Diego Ramos: Hi team, excited to walk through the SDKs today. we'll do Python quickstart, TS/Node, auth patterns, and then a console demo.
[00:18] Liam Chen: Thanks, we're mainly focused on latency for realtime fraud checks and cost for high-volume batch scoring.
[00:24] Maya Ortiz: also data residency and audit logs are important - we have compliance review next quarter.
[00:30] Aisha Patel: got it, we'll highlight Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and show how keys and KMS tie in. agenda: quickstarts, env setup, sample code, console, optimize.
[00:45] Diego Ramos: ok starting with Python quickstart - typical install is pip install redwood-inference (note: transcription may show package name slightly dif). locally you set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx.
[01:05] Diego Ramos: sample snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate("Summarize this transaction") - returns streaming token by default.
[01:25] Maya Ortiz: question: do you support key rotation and short-lived tokens? we prefer not to bake long-lived keys into containers.
[01:32] Aisha Patel: yes, short-lived tokens via our token exchange (can integrate with your IdP) and you can put customer-managed keys in our KMS integration for encryption-at-rest. Diego will show the env patterns.
[01:45] Diego Ramos: for Node/TS npm install @redwood/inference - then import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });
[02:05] Liam Chen: can you do a quick demo of the console auth settings? we use Okta, SAML/SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:12] Aisha Patel: yes, Redwood Console supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC roles, and audit logs tied to each request. Tina from security, you'll want the SOC 2 docs - we'll share those.
[02:28] Tina Alvarez: yes please include evidence for key rotation and audit logging retention periods.
[02:34] Diego Ramos: switching back to dev flow: for local dev we typically do a .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY, but recommend using a secrets manager in CI. for docker: pass the env var or mount a file; for k8s you can store in a secret and use projected volumes.
[02:50] Maya Ortiz: what's the difference in latency/cost between Hosted and Dedicated?
[02:56] Aisha Patel: Hosted is easiest and fast to start; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable p99 latency and lower unit cost at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for data residency/regulatory needs. Diego: can you mention the smart routing and fallback?
[03:10] Diego Ramos: sure — requests are routed by policy (latency, cost, region), and we have automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in case of capacity shortages. you can pin by model version for consistency.
[03:22] Liam Chen: do you support batching and caching? our throughput pattern has a lot of repeated prefixes.
[03:27] Diego Ramos: yes, Redwood Optimize suggests batching/caching config; we do prefix/KV cache to reduce token cost. also quantization profiles are suggested per workload.
[03:40] Jordan Price: any quick code for streaming in TS?
[03:43] Diego Ramos: yep — client.chat.stream(...) with an event emitter. small note: transcripts sometimes show stream as 'sting' but it's stream.
[03:55] Liam Chen: security: can you support VPC peering or private link?
[03:59] Aisha Patel: we support VPC peering and PrivateLink/privatelink-like setups for Private deployments, and an on-prem bundle if needed.
[04:10] Maya Ortiz: latency targets: we need <120ms p95 for a 256-token response in production. realistic?
[04:16] Diego Ramos: depends on model and quant; with Dedicated and optimized kernels we can get well under that for mid-size models; we'll run a benchmark with your sequences.
[04:28] Aisha Patel: ok demo time — switching to the Console: dashboards, per-route metrics, token cost breakdown, and rollouts. you can create an API key scoped to route or model and set quotas.
[04:45] Diego Ramos: click into a route, you'll see p50/p95 latencies, cost per token, and traces. you can configure canary deploys and automatic fallback policies.
[05:02] Liam Chen: can we limit a route to specific IPs?
[05:05] Aisha Patel: yes, via network policies and you can add allowlists at the route level.
[05:12] Maya Ortiz: about SDK versions — how stable are the Python/TS SDKs?
[05:16] Diego Ramos: they're stable; we follow semantic versioning and publish changelogs. the SDKs wrap the REST API and handle streaming, retries, and automatic token refresh helpers.
[05:28] Jordan Price: demo of sample app?
[05:30] Aisha Patel: we have a sample fraud-detection repo — we'll share that link. it shows batch scoring, real-time calls with websockets for streaming, and metrics integration.
[05:45] Diego Ramos: quick note on infra: if you go Dedicated, you get reserved capacity and autoscaling policies; for Private we provide a private control plane and you manage networking, plus HSM/KMS integrations.
[06:00] Liam Chen: our PCI team will want to see encryption in transit + at rest details and audit logs retained for 1 year.
[06:06] Tina Alvarez: yes, and proof of SOC2 type II.
[06:10] Aisha Patel: we'll attach the security pack and SOC 2 report.
[06:15] Maya Ortiz: okay, can you outline a recommended quickstart for our engineers? step-by-step please.
[06:20] Diego Ramos: sure: 1) create an org in Redwood Console, 2) create scoped API key or short-lived token for CI, 3) clone sample repo, 4) set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env, 5) run python app or node app locally, 6) run benchmark script we provide to collect p95/p99.
[06:40] Diego Ramos: sample python commands (spoken): pip install redwood-inference; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; python examples/quickstart.py. node: npm i @redwood/inference; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; node examples/quickstart.js.
[06:55] Liam Chen: can we set up a pilot with 100k monthly tokens and a small Dedicated tranche?
[07:00] Aisha Patel: yes we'll propose a pilot plan. we'll include pricing tiers.
[07:05] Jordan Price: what's the onboarding timeline?
[07:08] Aisha Patel: typical pilot 2-4 weeks for integration + benchmarks; Dedicated provisioning takes longer depending on GPU availability — usually 1-3 weeks after contract.
[07:18] Maya Ortiz: any caveats for Typescript strict mode?
[07:21] Diego Ramos: SDK has types, some deep edge typings for streams; we recommend using the latest TS and we'll share a tsconfig sample.
[07:30] Liam Chen: do you have rate limiting and backpressure built-in?
[07:33] Diego Ramos: yes, client side retries with jitter, server-side rate limiting and quotas. you can set per-route quotas in console.
[07:42] Aisha Patel: okay quick pause — a few questions from our side?
[07:46] Maya Ortiz: do you support webhooks for async jobs?
[07:49] Diego Ramos: yes, async job endpoints with webhook callbacks (we'll include the spec).
[07:56] Liam Chen: how do we do cost attribution across teams?
[08:00] Aisha Patel: Console has token-level cost breakdowns and tagging to map usage to projects.
[08:06] Maya Ortiz: any examples of large customers in payments?
[08:09] Aisha Patel: we have several payments customers (anonymized) and can share a case study.
[08:16] Diego Ramos: back to the tech — code snippet for token refresh: we provide a helper to exchange your IdP JWT for a short-lived Redwood token; avoids long-lived secrets in containers.
[08:30] Jordan Price: what's the recommended approach for caching repeated prefixes?
[08:33] Diego Ramos: use prefix/KV cache; we can configure on the route to cache first n tokens or do prefix matching; Optimize suggests cache sizes based on your distribution.
[08:45] Tina Alvarez: where are logs stored and how long?
[08:48] Aisha Patel: default retention 90 days; extended retention add-on available. audit logs are available via our API and can be exported to your logging bucket.
[09:00] Liam Chen: can you run a controlled benchmark with our sample workload?
[09:04] Aisha Patel: yes we'll run a pilot benchmark — Diego will coordinate.
[09:08] Diego Ramos: action: I'll prepare a benchmark script and sample sequences.
[09:12] Maya Ortiz: will the benchmark reflect production latencies?
[09:15] Diego Ramos: we'll run with similar batch sizes/seq lengths; for p95 we recommend Dedicated.
[09:22] Aisha Patel: wrapping up — recap and next steps.
[09:26] Diego Ramos: recap: shared quickstarts (Python/TS), security pack, sample repo, benchmark script, pilot pricing.
[09:32] Aisha Patel: next meeting — pilot kickoff, TBD. we'll aim to send materials by EOD tomorrow.
[09:38] Liam Chen: thanks everyone.
[09:40] Maya Ortiz: thanks.
[51:10] <<end of recording>>
